programs.name: utmconv
programs.purpose: Convert ASCII longitude and latitude coordinates to UTM coordinates or convert UTM coordinates back to longitude and latitude.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: UTMCONV - CONVert longitude and latitude to UTM, and vice versa

params.name: format
params.description: Printf-style format for each output coordinate; at most 20 characters.

params.name: a
params.default: computed: semimajor axis of the ellipsoid selected by idx
params.description: Positive ellipsoid semimajor axis in meters; overrides the selected ellipsoid's value.

params.name: f
params.default: computed: flattening of the ellipsoid selected by idx
params.description: Nonnegative ellipsoid flattening; overrides the selected ellipsoid's value.

params.name: letter
params.description: If nonzero, output or read a zone letter designator instead of a signed zone number.

params.name: invert
params.description: If nonzero, convert UTM coordinates to longitude and latitude; otherwise convert longitude and latitude to UTM.

params.name: verbose
params.description: If nonzero, report ellipsoid parameters and the number of converted coordinate pairs.

params.name: lon0
params.default: computed: central meridian from the UTM zone number
params.description: Override the central meridian in degrees; must be between -180 and 180.

params.name: ysoff
params.description: False northing for the southern hemisphere.

params.name: ynoff
params.description: False northing for the northern hemisphere.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Projection series use double-precision arithmetic and platform-dependent sin, cos, tan, sqrt, pow, and floor; evaluation order and fused operations can affect rounding. In inverse mode the zone is read as float and converted to short. The user-provided printf format is incorporated into a format string without validating its conversion specifiers, so incompatible formats can cause undefined behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program implements forward and inverse Transverse Mercator series, ellipsoid selection, and UTM zone and hemisphere rules.

test_cases.description: Convert northern and southern longitude/latitude pairs with signed zones; ASCII input is needed because the program does not consume SU traces.
test_cases.command: printf '14.125 40.822\n151.2 -33.8\n' | utmconv idx=23 format=%.3f letter=0 invert=0

test_cases.description: Exercise letter designators and special northern zones.
Convert signed UTM zones back to longitude and latitude with custom offsets and central meridian.
test_cases.command: printf '500000 0 31\n500000 10000000 -31\n' | utmconv invert=1 letter=0 lon0=3 xoff=500000 ynoff=0 ysoff=10000000 format=%.6f

test_cases.description: Round-trip a southern coordinate using letter designators and a user-specified spherical ellipsoid.
test_cases.command: printf '18 -34\n' | utmconv idx=0 a=6371000 f=0 letter=1 format=%.6f | utmconv invert=1 idx=0 a=6371000 f=0 letter=1 format=%.6f

programs.license_note: The forward and inverse projection routines state that they were adopted from a Perl routine in Geo-Coordinates-UTM-0.06 by G. Crookham; the file also cites NIMA and J. P. Snyder references.
